extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and examiners dealing with Eurasian (EAPO) patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and practical guidance on the requirement of unity of invention for Eurasian patent applications, including permitted claim groupings, search/examination practice, and the rights/requirements for filing divisional Eurasian applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of unity of invention (Rule 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Eurasian application shall relate to one invention only or to a group of inventions so linked as to form a single inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where one and the same Eurasian application relates to a group of inventions, the requirement of unity shall be deemed complied with only if there exists a technical relationship among those inventions involving one or more of the same or corresponding special technical features which define the contribution made over the prior art by each of the claimed inventions. If requirement not satisfied applicant must limit the application to one invention or to a group that satisfy unity and may file divisional applications for other inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of technical relationship / special technical features
rubrics_metrics.description: A technical relationship among inventions involving one or more of the same or corresponding special technical features; that is, those technical features which define the contribution made over the prior art by each of the claimed inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The special technical feature is considered with respect to novelty and inventive step. The special feature need not be literally identical in each invention; corresponding special technical features that provide the same technical effect can suffice. If the only common feature linking claims is known from the prior art, there is no technical relationship and no unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted multiple claim categories in one application (Rule 25)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to Rule 4, a Eurasian application may contain independent claims relating to different categories (e.g., device, substance/biotechnological product, a process specially adapted for making the device/substance/product, and a use of the device/substance/product).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: (i) independent claims for a device/product, for a process of making it, and for the use of it; (ii) a process claim and a device specially adapted for carrying out that process; (iii) two or more independent claims of the same category characterizing variants correlated as part and whole. Inclusion of different categories is allowed only if unity per Rule 4 is satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination and search of unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity of invention is examined both in search and examination procedures; lack of unity may be determined a priori (before starting the search) in evident cases or a posteriori after taking into account the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Claims: 1) Compound X; 2) Process of manufacturing X; 3) Use of X. If Compound X is unknown from the prior art it is the special feature and unity is satisfied. If Compound X is known from the prior art, it cannot be the special feature contributing over the prior art and there is no unity between claims 2 and 3; an objection of lack of unity should be raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when lack of unity is found during search
rubrics_metrics.description: If lack of unity is found during the search, the applicant is invited, within two months of the notification date, to pay an additional fee or to state the invention(s) with respect to which the search is to be carried out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant does not pay the additional fee or does not state which invention(s) shall be the subject of search, the patent search is carried out only in relation to the invention, or group of inventions forming a general inventive concept, mentioned first in the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of lack of unity for opposition/revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of unity is no ground for opposition or revocation of a Eurasian patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In opposition/revocation proceedings the requirement of unity of invention is not considered for a patent maintained in amended form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to file divisional Eurasian application (Rule 49(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Eurasian application as originally filed contains other inventions, the applicant has the right to file a divisional Eurasian application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A divisional application shall enjoy the filing date and, where appropriate, the priority date of the parent application from which it was divided, provided it has been filed only in relation to inventions disclosed in the parent application and the information in the divisional does not go beyond the parent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional claims must not duplicate parent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims of a divisional Eurasian application shall not contain inventions identical to the inventions for which legal protection is requested in the parent Eurasian application, except in the case of limitation of the parent application in accordance with Rule 4 where unity was violated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibits claiming the same subject-matter with the same scope in the divisional as in the parent, unless the parent has been limited under Rule 4; examiners will check for identity of claimed scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and conditions for filing a divisional application
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional application may be filed if on its filing date the parent application has not been withdrawn or is not considered withdrawn, and its filing is prior to the date of grant of the Eurasian patent for the parent application or, where a decision of refusal has been taken, until the possibility for appeal has been exhausted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical note: The divisional may be filed while the parent is pending, or not later than the date of publication of the mention to grant the Eurasian patent, or, where a decision of refusal has been taken, until the appeal possibilities are exhausted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application formal status and chaining
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional application is filed directly with the EAPO and is regarded as a new Eurasian application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A divisional application may be divided in turn; in this case the first divisional is a parent application for the second divisional. The divisional enjoys filing and, where appropriate, priority dates of the parent if it meets the disclosure and content-limitation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for divisional to enjoy parent's filing/priority date
rubrics_metrics.description: The divisional application is entitled to the filing date and priority date of the parent only if: (i) it is filed only in relation to subject-matter disclosed in the parent application and which does not go beyond the content of the parent application; and (ii) the divisional does not claim an invention identical (with respect to claimed scope) to the invention contained in claims of the parent application or the Eurasian patent granted on its basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the filed divisional does not comply with these requirements the applicant is notified to submit claims consistent with Rule 49(6) within two months; failure to do so will result in the divisional being deemed withdrawn, although further processing and restoration of rights are provided for in such a case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and time limits for amending non-compliant divisional claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the filed divisional application does not comply with the divisional requirements, the applicant is notified about the necessity to submit claims consistent with Rule 49(6) within two months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant does not submit amended claims within this time limit the divisional Eurasian application shall be deemed withdrawn. Further processing and restoration of rights are available subject to EAPO rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical example illustrating unity determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Example given: Claim 1: Compound X. Claim 2: Process of manufacturing compound X. Claim 3: Use of compound X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If compound X is unknown from the prior art it is the special feature contributing over the prior art and unity across claims 1–3 is satisfied. If compound X is known from the prior art it cannot be considered a special feature and there is no unity between claims 2 and 3; an objection of lack of unity should be raised.
